title: Anti-symmetrization is cheap and useful
authors: Adam Bene Watts, John Bostanci, Matthias C. Caro, Daniel Grier, Sihan Liu, Gaurav Mahajan
abstract: We consider the computational task of anti-symmetrization of an unknown mixed quantum state: Given iid copies of a rank-$r$ qudit state $ρ=\sum_{i=1}^r λ_i |\varphi_i\rangle\!\langle\varphi_i|$, prepare a copy of the state proportional to $Π_{\mathrm{anti}}^r (|\varphi_1\rangle\otimes \ldots\otimes|\varphi_r\rangle)$, with $Π_{\mathrm{anti}}^r$ the anti-symmetric subspace projector. We first give a simple algorithm for anti-symmetrization that uses $\widetilde{O}(r / λ_{\min})$ copies of $ρ$, where $λ_{\min}$ is the minimum non-zero eigenvalue of $ρ$. This algorithm works even in the streaming setting with small working memory, and it uses only simple quantum operations like controlled-SWAPs and constantly many layers of single-qubit gates. As an application of this streaming anti-symmetrization procedure, we give a reduction from gapped mixed-state one-way state generators to pure-state one-way state generators. Then, using tools from Schur-Weyl duality, we give and analyze a second (non-streaming) anti-symmetrization procedure that uses $O(r / λ_{\min})$ copies of $ρ$, which then serves as a building block in new algorithms for weak Schur sampling and unitary Schur sampling, outperforming existing approaches in some regimes of number of copies $n$ and local dimension $d$, as well as in an algorithm for optimal purity amplification for qudit states.
summary: This work introduces efficient quantum algorithms for performing anti-symmetrization on mixed quantum states. By developing both streaming and copy-reusing procedures, the authors provide improved resource estimates for key quantum tasks. These results advance the understanding of how to prepare highly entangled, anti-symmetric quantum states for applications in quantum sampling and state purification.
main_problem: The paper focuses on developing efficient quantum algorithms to perform anti-symmetrization on unknown mixed quantum states.
main_result: They present algorithms achieving sample complexities of O(r/lambda_min) for anti-symmetrization, which are then used to improve weak/unitary Schur sampling and purity amplification protocols.
method: The methods involve developing streaming and non-streaming quantum circuits, leveraging tools from representation theory (Schur-Weyl duality) to analyze the state preparation.
model_or_system: The system involves mixed qudit states $\rho$ with rank $r$, and the goal is to project onto the anti-symmetric subspace $\Pi_{\text{anti}}^r$. The analysis uses concepts from the representation theory of the symmetric group.
key_observables: Sample complexity ($n$), gate complexity (controlled-SWAP operations, T-count), and the resulting state proportional to the anti-symmetric projector.
important_parameters: Rank of the state ($r$), minimum non-zero eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\min}$), local dimension ($d$), and desired accuracy ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on advanced tools from representation theory (e.g., Pieri's rule) and assumes the validity of previous results regarding projector structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the anti-symmetrization task and presenting initial streaming algorithms, to developing more complex, copy-reusing procedures, and finally using representation theory to rigorously analyze the resulting state structure for applications like Schur sampling.
why_interesting: The techniques developed for state preparation and sampling are fundamental building blocks for quantum simulation and quantum computation protocols, especially those involving entanglement structure.
